subject: SIG questionnaire: follow-up on contingency / backup & RTO/RPO evidence
messages:
From: Kevin Li <kevin.li@medtechinc.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: GRC Team <gct@medtechinc.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up: clarifications on RTO/RPO, backups and regional failover

Markus —

Thanks again for the SIG package you sent last week. Our security assessment team finished an initial pass and has a few follow-up questions specifically around business continuity and disaster recovery sections (RTO/RPO, backup retention, cross-region failover). We want to get this answered ahead of our vendor review board next Thursday.

Top-line asks:
- Can you confirm the Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) ranges for the hosted Redwood API (managed offering) vs Dedicated seats?
- Where are backups stored, how long are snapshots retained, and can you provide an extract (policy snippet) that cites encryption-at-rest and access controls?
- Do you support automated cross-region failover for customer workloads, and if so, what is the documented failover sequence?

If possible, please attach the short summary and any network/architecture diagram that shows region failover. A one-page summary would be ideal for our board packet.

Appreciate it — can we get responses by EOD Tuesday (11/10)?

Kevin
Kevin Li
IT GRC — MedTech, Inc.

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Kevin Li <kevin.li@medtechinc.com>
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: clarifications on RTO/RPO, backups and regional failover

Kevin —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers; I attached a short one-page summary (redwood_bcp_rto_rpo_summary.pdf), an architecture diagram for region failover (aws-region-failover-diagram.png), and a policy excerpt (backup-policy-snippet.txt) that pulls the retention and encryption language. Short answers first, then a couple of notes.

1) RTO / RPO
- Hosted API: Typical RTO target 15–30 minutes for control-plane failover with automatic routing to healthy pools; RPO is up to 1 minute for active request state due to continuous KV caching and checkpointed snapshots.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): RTO target 30–120 minutes depending on the customer's validation window and whether they have cross-region replication enabled; RPO default is up to 5 minutes (customers can choose more frequent snapshot cadence as part of their agreement).

Notes: Targets are SLO-focused and depend on the customer's deployment (single-region vs cross-region). For enterprise Dedicated customers we include tailored runbooks and an agreed RTO/RPO in the service addendum.

2) Backups and retention
- Snapshot storage: encrypted snapshots stored in customer-dedicated buckets (hosted) or customer-managed buckets (Private). All snapshots use AES-256 at rest; keys managed via KMS (Redwood supports AWS KMS or customer HSM).
- Retention: Default retention is 30 days for hot snapshots, 90 days for warm snapshots, and cold archive retention is configurable up to 365 days. The attached backup-policy-snippet.txt shows the exact retention table and the IAM roles allowed to restore.

3) Regional failover
- Automated cross-region failover is supported for Hosted and for Dedicated with cross-region replication enabled. Sequence (high level):
  a) Health detection triggers automated routing change (control-plane) to standby region.
  b) DNS + routing propagation (global load balancers) begin within seconds; full traffic shaping occurs within target RTO window noted above as services are warmed via cached prefix replay.
  c) State reconciliation uses last snapshot + transaction log replay to reach target RPO.
- The attached diagram illustrates an active->standby failover between us-west-2 and eu-central-1.

If you need explicit runbook steps (playbook with on-call run actions) I can loop in SRE to provide an ops-level document.

Let me know if that hits the board ask or if you want us on a short sync.

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

--
Attachments: redwood_bcp_rto_rpo_summary.pdf, aws-region-failover-diagram.png, backup-policy-snippet.txt

This is very helpful, thank you. A couple of quick clarifications the board specifically requested after reviewing your summary:

- For Dedicated RTO ranges (30–120m) can you confirm what factors push a deployment toward the 120m end (example: large dataset restores, manual DNS approvals, or capacity constraints)?

Also, would you be able to provide a sanitized sample restore playbook that shows the steps your SREs run (no customer-identifying data needed) — or alternatively confirm we can review the full runbook under NDA? The board likes to see ops-level steps when they approve vendor risk.

If you can get back by 5pm PT today that would be ideal for our packet.

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: clarifications on RTO/RPO, backups and regional failover

Kevin —

Following up with the extra detail you requested:

- Hosted RPO: The ~1 minute RPO is an operational SLO for our hosted control plane and is achieved via continuous KV checkpointing and write-ahead log (WAL) upload frequency. It is classified as "best-effort SLO" in our public docs; for security reviews we describe it that way and include measured median/95th-percentile figures in the SIEM summary. For contractual guarantees we offer Dedicated customers explicit RPOs in the service addendum.

- Dedicated RTO factors: The 120 minute upper bound typically occurs when customers require: large-state full restores (multi-TB), manual human approvals for DNS cutover, or if cross-region replication wasn't pre-warmed and needs bulk replay. If a customer elects continuous cross-region replication and pre-warmed standby, they usually operate near the lower bound. We can include a small table in the deliverable that maps configuration choices to expected RTO.

- Restore playbook: We can provide a sanitized ops playbook. We cannot share internal runbooks verbatim without an NDA, but we can provide a redacted sample playbook that lists step-by-step actions, required IAM roles, estimated time per step, and checkpoints. If you sign our standard mutual NDA (link below) we can share the full runbook.

Deliverables attached: sanitized-restore-playbook-sample.txt (inside backup-policy-snippet.txt archive) and the previously attached files.

Links: 
- NDA (sample): https://redwood.app/legal/mutual-nda
- HubSpot record (for tracking): https://redwood.app/hubspot/record/HD-1287
